analyst.summary: Tech Mahindra's June-quarter results confirmed its margin turnaround is real and on schedule - profitability keeps improving quarter after quarter, and the company continues to win new business at a healthy pace. But the part of the business that should be growing revenue, its telecom/communications work (its single largest client vertical), barely grew at all this quarter, and overall revenue growth remains the slowest among its large peers. The share price has already run up meaningfully in anticipation of the margin story finishing well, so at current levels an investor is paying close to full price for a turnaround that still has real execution risk left in it, with a core growth engine that has not yet turned around. We rate this a Sell - not because the company is doing badly, but because the good news already looks priced in while the main growth lever still isn't working.
